RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 30

The all-male panel is not evidence of discrimination by itself — it's context that matters only if the decision itself looks unsound. On its own it proves nothing; plenty of all-male panels appoint women.

So don't lead with it. Lead with the unanswered request: a public broadcaster failing to give written reasons after two weeks is a concrete procedural failure, and it's the thing most likely to get you answers. Ask specifically how "digital media experience" was weighted, when that criterion was set, and against what scoring.

Mention the panel composition later, as part of a pattern, if the reasons turn out to be vague or the criterion looks retrofitted. Raised too early, it lets them argue about your motives instead of their process.
